description: Ranks cards the user doesn't have by what they'd be worth over the first two years: what each adds to the user's cards (or, with none, earns) on their spending, plus the public welcome (sign-up) bonus in year one if its minimum spend fits in the window, less each year's annual fee. A card that needs a membership the user hasn't given (Verizon Visa) is left out of the ranking and named after it, in `membersOnly`. Each offer also shows the bonus alone (first-year value), year one and year two, and how many weeks of spending the minimum takes. Offers the issuer rules out because of a card in the user's wallet are marked likely not eligible and listed last; issuers the user can't get cards from (skippedIssuers, or saved with set_memberships) are left out. Use it when the user asks which card to get next or which has the best sign-up bonus. Spending is optional (typical amounts otherwise). It covers only the cards earnrate knows, offers vary by person, and each offer's note gives the issuer's eligibility rules; pass those caveats on. Never suggest applying through a link.

business.description: Business cards instead of personal ones.

cards.description: Cards the user named in this conversation, to answer for just those cards without saving anything. Leave out to use the user's saved wallet if they have one; with neither, the answer covers every card earnrate knows.

activated.description: Bonuses the user has activated with the issuer, as rule ids from search_cards.

enrolled.description: Statement credits the user has enrolled in with the issuer, and free nights they use, as ids from search_cards. A credit that needs enrolling counts only when it's here. Ask; never assume.

opened.description: The day the account opened (YYYY-MM-DD), for a card with a first-year rate. Optional; without it the card is ranked at its standard rates.

picks.description: Bonus categories the user picked, for cards that have them: choice id → option ids, from search_cards. Ask; don't guess.

skippedCredits.description: Statement credit and free night ids the user says they don't use. They don't count toward a pick or against the card's annual fee.

includeHeld.description: Include cards already in the wallet.

kind.description: cash: cash back cards only. points: points and miles cards only.

memberships.description: Memberships the user has, such as amazon-prime or costco, when they're named in the conversation rather than saved.

noAnnualFee.description: Only cards with no annual fee.

skippedIssuers.description: Issuers the user says they can't or won't get a new card from (for example Chase, over its 5/24 rule), for this answer. Replaces the saved list. Never assume it.

spending.description: Monthly spending lines, each a category (grocery.supermarket, dining, gas, other) or a merchant (Amazon, Costco). Optional: leave out to use typical amounts, and don't press the user for numbers they haven't offered.

category.description: A spending category: dining (Restaurants), dining.fast_food (Fast food), grocery.supermarket (Supermarkets), grocery.online (Online grocery and delivery), superstore (Superstores), warehouse_club (Warehouse clubs), convenience_store (Convenience stores), gas (Gas stations), gas.grocery_store (Gas at grocery stores), gas.superstore (Gas at superstores and warehouse clubs), ev_charging (EV charging), transit (Transit), transit.rideshare (Rideshare and taxis), travel (Travel), travel.flights (Flights), travel.hotels (Hotels), travel.car_rental (Car rentals), travel.cruise (Cruises), streaming (Streaming services), tv_internet (TV and internet service), phone (Cell phone service), utilities (Home utilities), housing (Rent and mortgage), drugstore (Drugstores and pharmacies), movie_theaters (Movie theaters), entertainment (Live entertainment and events), fitness (Gyms and fitness), department_store (Department stores), clothing (Clothing stores), electronics (Electronics stores), sporting_goods (Sporting goods stores), home_improvement (Home improvement), furniture (Furniture stores), online_retail (Online retail), office_supply (Office supply stores), shipping (Shipping and couriers), online_advertising (Social media and search advertising), other (Everything else).

merchant.description: Merchant name or web address as the user would say it or see it, e.g. "Whole Foods" or "delta.com", or a kind of place, e.g. "restaurants" or "gas station".

valuation.description: Instead of the user's saved point values (or earnrate's defaults): flat, points at their cash-out value, MR and UR at 1¢; or points-heavy, MR and UR at 1.7¢, for people who transfer points to airlines and hotels.
